signals.title: NOK/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: NOK leads the weekly G10 scorecard up +1.128% across 2 pairs, while USD lags at −0.469% across 9 pairs, opening a 1.597% bilateral spread. Norges Bank policy rate sits at 4.5% with a +1.82% real policy rate, compared to the Fed at 4.0% with a +1.67% real policy rate. USD/NOK trades at 9.459, holding below its SMA20 of 9.530 and SMA200 of 9.536. Spot weakness persists despite retail positioning showing an extreme 100% long bias, creating conditions for contrarian acceleration lower. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK; policy divergence and weekly momentum favor continued Krone outperformance. Catalyst: Norges Bank policy meeting 5 Nov. Risk: Norges Bank signals an earlier easing cycle while US data surprises higher, unwinding NOK relative strength.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Macro Divergence + Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.95, holding between its SMA50 at 157.71 and SMA200 at 158.55 while 160.00 remains the key level for verbal intervention risk. Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% provides a +265bp OIS carry advantage to the dollar, yet BoJ Governor Ueda signaled underlying inflation risks overshooting 2% and reiterated intentions to keep hiking. Saxo 1M 25d risk reversals print at −1.90, reflecting pronounced put skew and institutional demand for downside protection. CFTC data shows leveraged funds holding JPY net short −30,379 contracts at the 90th percentile of its 52-week range, indicating short positioning remains stretched. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; hawkish central bank messaging and elevated downside options skew outweigh baseline carry. Catalyst: BoJ rate decision 30 Oct. Risk: BoJ leaves policy unadjusted without forward guidance, allowing the +265bp carry spread to reassert upward spot momentum.
evidence: 25d RR: -1.90 put skew (Saxo, 1M tenor, indicative mid)

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Event Risk
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1237, positioned below its SMA20 at 1.1299 and SMA50 at 1.1478. CFTC leveraged funds hold EUR net short −84,775 contracts at the 4th percentile of the 52-week range, with z-score at −1.64 reflecting a heavily stretched short exposure. The OIS spread of +144bp favors the dollar based on SOFR 3.88% versus €STR 2.44%, yet short-covering risks dominate as selling momentum decelerates. Implied volatility runs at 6.2% against HV30 of 4.2%, establishing a +1.9% volatility risk premium ahead of immediate macroeconomic releases. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD; stretched speculative short exposure limits sustained downside continuation. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI y/y release at 09:00 UTC. Risk: Euro Area Core CPI falls significantly below 2.5%, validating spec shorts and resuming downward trend toward 1.1100.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Technical Compression + Rates Divergence
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3310, hovering directly above its SMA20 of 1.3256 but constrained beneath the SMA50/200 cluster at 1.3422/1.3435. BoE at 3.75% matches against Fed 4.00% for a modest 25bp policy rate gap, with UK-US 2Y yield spreads steady at −6bp. Governor Bailey noted subdued second-round inflation pressures despite market pricing for a November hike, checking Sterling momentum. Speculative positioning shows leveraged funds net long +6,063 contracts at the 8th percentile of the 52-week distribution, indicating institutional long participation has largely cleared out. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD; technical moving-average boundaries contain directional expansion. Catalyst: BoE meeting 5 Nov. Risk: US industrial production data triggers a broad USD breakout past technical moving averages.
evidence: BoE 3.75% vs Fed 4.00% — 25bp carry favor USD
